kilauea_notices.title: HAWAIIAN VOLCANO OBSERVATORY DAILY UPDATE
kilauea_notices.message: HVO Kilauea ORANGE/WATCH - A shallow intrusion of magma occurred overnight within the summit region near the existing eruption location. North and south vent continue to have intermittent overflows, spatter, and strong glow. There is no anomalous activity outside of the summit.
kilauea_notices.detail: Overview: Over the past 24 hours, north and south vent continued to have intermittent overflows and spattering, with strong glow and flames emitted overnight. As this eruptive activity continued, a shallow intrusion of magma with an east-west orientation occurred within the summit region overnight near the existing eruption location. Intrusive activity was strongest between 8 p.m. H.S.T. last night (September 30, 2026) and this morning around 3 a.m. H.S.T. The intrusive activity was recorded by large rapid displacements on the summit tiltmeters, increased earthquake activity in summit region, and increased tremor. There is no evidence that magma associated with this intrusion erupted in a new location. Episode 55 fountaining remains a possibility during the ongoing Kīlauea summit eruption. In the past 24 hours, north vent had several overflows that included a small dome fountain, including an overflow that lasted over an hour yesterday afternoon. During the overnight intrusion, north and south vents exhibited strong glow, intermittent spatter, and large flames; west vent also had glow and large flames. North vent also had several large overflows during the intrusion. South vent overflows resumed after intrusive activity ended. No anomalous seismic activity or deformation has occurred outside of the summit region, and no significant activity has been noted along Kīlauea’s East Rift Zone or Southwest Rift Zone. STATUS REPORT published during intrusive activity: https://volcanoes.usgs.gov/hans-public/notice/DOI-USGS-HVO-2026-10-01T08:14:21+00:00 STATUS REPORT on changes in activity and implications for this eruption: https://volcanoes.usgs.gov/hans-public/notice/DOI-USGS-HVO-2026-09-15T03:18:09+00:00 NOTE: Significant changes in activity between Daily Updates are posted here: https://www.usgs.gov/observatories/hvo/observatory-messages Summit Observations: Overflows from the north vent resumed on the evening of September 22 after about 10 days of quiescence at the vent complex. Overflow activity from the south vent began on September 27. However, the north vent remained dominant until the evening of September 28, when south vent started having short, rapid cycles of overflows and lava drainback that continued through yesterday afternoon. These south vent overflows lasted about 2–5 minutes, with most pauses between each cycle lasting about 5–7 minutes; there were over 100 such overflows. Since September 29, the frequency of overflow activity has greatly decreased, although intermittent overflows continue at both north and south vents. Since yesterday September 30, north vent has had several overflows with minor dome fountaining. Eruptions from the north and south vents stopped during the early stages of dike emplaced yesterday afternoon, but the north vent resumed later during continued intrusive activity. The south vent had at least one overflow this morning after intrusive activity quieted down. In total, there were at least 10 overflows during and after the main intrusive event. Both north and south vents also spattered overnight and had persistent strong glow, and west vent had occasional glow. No other areas of incandescence were observed across the summit region last night. Increased earthquake activity began yesterday, September 30, 2026, at approximately 2 p.m. HST, underneath Halemaʻumaʻu. In the past 24 hours, there were 98 shallow earthquakes located across the summit region, primarily underneath Halemaʻumaʻu, the largest of which was a magnitude (M) 3.4 earthquake at 9:52 p.m. H.S.T. Starting around 8 p.m. HST., summit tiltmeters began to show extremely rapid changes consistent with crack growth in an east-west orientation near the current vent area, suggesting that magma was intruding in this region. Most of the seismicity was confined to the western part of Halemaʻumaʻu and the northwestern part of Kaluapele, the summit caldera. mauna_loa_notices.title: HAWAIIAN VOLCANO OBSERVATORY MONTHLY UPDATE
mauna_loa_notices.message: HVO Mauna Loa GREEN/NORMAL - Mauna Loa earthquake counts decreased in September compared to August, and minor inflation continues.
mauna_loa_notices.detail: Mauna Loa had a decrease in seismic activity compared to the previous month; a total of 53 earthquakes were detected in Mauna Loa's summit region during the September reporting period, after 87 in August. Most earthquakes occurred deep beneath the upper Southwest Rift Zone or broadly scattered around the upper flanks. No earthquakes occurred directly beneath Mokuʻāweoweo. Data from Global Positioning System (GPS) instruments on Mauna Loa showed slight inflation across the summit region in the past month. Oscillations between contraction and inflation patterns during non-eruptive periods are normal, but inflation has been the dominant trend since the 2022 eruption, consistent with magma refilling the summit reservoir system. Gas and temperature data from a station on Mauna Loa's Southwest Rift Zone indicate these values are at background levels, with little change relative to previous months. HVO continues to closely monitor Mauna Loa and will issue another update in one month, or earlier, should conditions change significantly.
